feature.title: From Bench to Bedside: TCT 2026 Caps a Year of Landmark Medtech Deployments and Trial Readouts
feature.summary: Today marks the final day of TCT 2026 in San Diego, where the cardiology world receives the PROTEMBO IDE trial's final results on cerebral embolic protection during TAVR — one of 28 late-breaking studies at the conference. The readout arrives alongside a year of historic medtech deployments: J&J's OTTAVA robot cleared for ten general surgery procedures and now commercially launching, Aidoc's AI platform processing 60 million cases annually across 1,600+ hospitals, and Abbott's Libre Duo dual glucose-ketone sensor becoming the world's first device to continuously track both analytes. The macro theme of 2026 is unmistakable: clinical AI and novel devices are no longer in pilot mode — measurable real-world outcomes data now validates them at scale. Across robotics, diagnostics, genomics, and wearables, the evidential bar has risen from FDA clearance to proven patient impact.

highlights.label: Biggest story
highlights.text: TCT 2026 closes today with the PROTEMBO IDE final results and the landmark PROGRESS trial data on TAVR vs. surveillance for moderate aortic stenosis — both set to reset structural heart practice guidelines.

highlights.label: Key trend
highlights.text: Hospital-deployed AI is now producing hard outcome numbers: City of Hope cut surgical complication rates from 58.8% to 46%, Aidoc's sepsis AI reduced in-hospital mortality by 39.5% across 9 hospitals, and Viz.ai slashed LVO stroke door-to-door time by 44%.

highlights.label: To watch
highlights.text: Precision BioSciences' PBGENE-HBV ELIMINATE-B trial oral presentation at AASLD on November 8 could be the year's most important gene-editing clinical readout.

articles.title: PROTEMBO IDE Trial Final Results Presented at TCT 2026: Cerebral Protection During TAVR Under the Microscope
articles.snippet: The final results of the randomized PROTEMBO IDE trial — evaluating the ProtEmbo cerebral embolic protection device against hybrid controls during TAVR — were presented today, November 3, at TCT 2026 in San Diego by Susheel Kodali. The trial compared new brain lesion volumes via DW-MRI at 36 hours post-procedure, with earlier feasibility data showing 87% of patients had no single lesion exceeding 150mm³ and a 94.6% device success rate with no deaths or device-related adverse events.
articles.result: 87% of TAVR patients showed no large brain lesion post-procedure

articles.title: PROGRESS Trial Primary Results: TAVR vs. Clinical Surveillance in 2,250 Moderate Aortic Stenosis Patients
articles.snippet: The PROGRESS randomized trial — comparing TAVR to watchful waiting in 2,250 symptomatic patients with moderate aortic stenosis — delivered its primary results at TCT 2026 on November 2 in collaboration with the New England Journal of Medicine. The trial could redefine when clinicians intervene, challenging the established threshold of waiting until aortic stenosis becomes severe before offering transcatheter valve replacement.
articles.result: Primary results from 2,250-patient TAVR timing trial published in NEJM

articles.title: J&J OTTAVA Surgical Robot: FDA-Authorized and Commercially Launching After Meeting All Pivotal Endpoints
articles.snippet: Johnson & Johnson received FDA De Novo authorization for the OTTAVA robotic surgical system in July 2026, covering ten general surgery procedures including gastric bypass, gastrectomy, and cholecystectomy. A pivotal multicenter study showed all procedures completed robotically without conversion, average 30-day weight loss of 30 pounds, and 100% of surveyed surgeons agreed OTTAVA can convert compact rooms into robotic suites.
articles.result: All cases completed robotically; 30-lb average weight loss at 30 days

articles.title: Aidoc CARE Foundation Model: 97% Sensitivity Across 14 Conditions, Now in 1,600+ Hospitals
articles.snippet: Aidoc's CARE multi-condition AI triage model — cleared by the FDA in January 2026 for body CT — achieved 97% mean sensitivity and 98% mean specificity across 14 acute findings in its pivotal study, and is now deployed across more than 1,600 hospitals processing 60 million patient cases annually. Germany's Asklepios Group completed one of Europe's largest clinical AI rollouts, deploying Aidoc's aiOS across 28 hospitals analyzing 35,000+ CT and X-ray images monthly.

articles.title: Abbott Libre Duo 10 Day: FDA Authorizes World's First Dual Glucose-Ketone Wearable Sensor
articles.snippet: The FDA authorized Abbott's Libre Duo 10 Day in August 2026 — the first wearable anywhere to continuously monitor both glucose and ketones in a single sensor, cleared for patients aged 2 and older. Authorization followed six clinical studies enrolling more than 600 participants; results showed the device accurately tracked rising ketone levels before DKA onset, with 84.1% of adult sensors lasting the full 10-day wear period.
articles.result: DKA-onset ketone elevation detected; 84.1% full 10-day sensor completion

articles.title: REVA Medical MOTIV BTK Trial: Bioresorbable Scaffold Shows 22-Point Patency Advantage Over Balloon Angioplasty
articles.snippet: REVA Medical's pivotal MOTIV BTK randomized trial met both primary safety and efficacy endpoints, with 12-month vessel patency of 70% for the sirolimus-eluting bioresorbable scaffold vs. 48% for balloon angioplasty — a 22% absolute improvement in a complex CLTI population. Late-breaking subgroup data were presented at VIVA26 in Las Vegas in October, and a live below-the-knee revascularization case was successfully demonstrated at the conference.
articles.result: 70% vs. 48% 12-month patency: 22-point absolute superiority over angioplasty

articles.title: CAR-T Therapy Azer-cel Shows Stable or Improved Disability in 89% of Progressive MS Patients
articles.snippet: TG Therapeutics presented the first clinical evaluation of an allogeneic CD19-directed CAR T-cell therapy in progressive multiple sclerosis at MSToronto2026 on October 23, 2026. Azer-cel demonstrated an encouraging preliminary safety profile with no high-grade CAR-T toxicities, and 89% of evaluable participants had stable or improved disability scores at Day 90 despite documented progression on prior high-efficacy therapies.
articles.result: 89% of progressive MS patients stable or improved at Day 90; zero high-grade toxicities

articles.title: City of Hope AI Risk Model Cuts Surgical Complications in Cancer Patients from 58.8% to 46%
articles.source: Association of Health Care Journalists / Health Journalism
articles.snippet: Surgical oncologist Lily Lai at City of Hope reported that a predictive AI tool embedded in patient EHR charts has reduced severe complication rates among high-risk cancer surgery patients from 58.8% to 46%, as discussed at AHCJ's fall summit in Los Angeles on October 29, 2026. The tool generates a pre-operative risk score from the top 10 complication risk factors, enabling surgeons to optimize or defer surgery in high-risk cases.
articles.result: Complication rate fell from 58.8% to 46% in high-risk cancer surgical patients

articles.title: AI Sepsis Algorithm Deployed Across 9 Hospitals Cuts In-Hospital Mortality by 39.5%
articles.source: Dialog Health / AI in Healthcare Statistics 2026
articles.snippet: A prospective evaluation across nine hospitals found that following deployment of a clinical AI sepsis detection algorithm, in-hospital mortality fell 39.5%, length of stay dropped 32.27%, and 30-day readmission declined 22.74%. Separately, a 2026 study showed Viz.ai's stroke AI reduced door-in-door-out time for large vessel occlusion patients by 44% at participating centers.
articles.result: In-hospital mortality down 39.5%; LOS down 32.27% across 9 hospitals

articles.title: Google AMIE AI in Real-World Primary Care: 114 Patients, Zero Safety Stops in Landmark Lancet Study
articles.snippet: A prospective real-world study of Google's AMIE conversational AI deployed in primary care at BIDMC — described as the first of its kind — enrolled 114 patients with zero safety stops triggered, publishing results in The Lancet on October 8, 2026. Patient attitudes toward AI improved significantly after the pre-visit chat (p<0.001), and the improvement persisted after the physician encounter, though direct patient outcome changes remain to be measured in follow-on work.
articles.result: 114 patients, zero safety stops; patient AI attitude improved significantly (p<0.001)

articles.title: Philips Future Health Index 2026: AI Now Saves Clinicians 132+ Hours Per Year as Adoption Hits Near-Universal Levels
articles.snippet: Philips' Future Health Index 2026 survey of U.S. healthcare professionals found that nearly half of clinicians now save at least 132 hours per year through AI tools — the equivalent of more than three working weeks. Additionally, 27% of healthcare professionals reported that AI helped them identify or prevent a potential medical error at least three times in the past three months, catching missed diagnoses and unsafe drug interactions before they reached patients.
articles.result: 132+ hours/year saved per clinician; 27% caught ≥3 medical errors in 3 months

articles.title: China Provincial Hospital AI Rollout: Waiting Time Cut from 18 to 13 Minutes, Patient Satisfaction Reaches 98.92%
articles.snippet: A published 18-month real-world study of three clinical AI pathways deployed in a Chinese provincial hospital system showed patient waiting time fell from 18 to 13 minutes post-deployment, while patient satisfaction rose to 98.92% (n=3,847 surveyed encounters). The AI rollout covered an intelligent pre-consultation system, a multidisciplinary tumor decision-support system, and a therapeutic drug-monitoring pathway, with daily utilization exceeding 100 encounters after phased rollout.
articles.result: Wait time: 18→13 min; satisfaction rose to 98.92% across 3,847 encounters
